key_insight: DynamicRubric argues that as LLM policies improve and candidate answers become closer in quality, evaluators must co-evolve to preserve useful relative score gaps for policy learning.
engineering_relevance: For production LLM training, this suggests adaptive evaluators can provide stronger supervision than static reward models when optimizing high-performing models on near-tied responses.
method: Condition the evaluator on the full response set, not each answer in isolation.
Generate weighted binary rubric items tailored to the candidate set.
Aggregate rubric judgments into response-level scores to drive policy updates.
evidence_signal: With 8B backbones, DynamicRubric outperforms baselines using a 70B reward model and a 235B static rubric generator, and the optimized policy improves verifiable reasoning and coding tasks.
watch_item: Because the method depends on response-set-conditioned rubrics, its effectiveness may be sensitive to rubric quality, calibration, and deployment cost at scale.
paper_title: Co-Evolving LLM Evaluators and Policies via DynamicRubric
